risks.note: Tea and rubber cultivation is fundamentally exposed to unpredictable weather and accelerating climate-change impacts, requiring continuous evolution of harvesting and cultivation practices.
Both tea and rubber are exceptionally labour-intensive and governed by stringent regulatory frameworks that complicate daily operations.
Margin pressure stems from escalating labour expenses, mandatory social welfare and infrastructure investments, and inflationary energy and raw material costs.
Acute seasonal labour deficits in specific geographies disrupt operational momentum during critical harvest windows.

The unorganized plantation sector, accounting for ~52% of the market, operates outside Plantation Labour Act welfare mandates, giving it a structural cost advantage over HML as a fully compliant organized-sector player.
Broader macroeconomic risks including volatile global markets and aggressive competition from rival exporting nations affect realizations and export demand.
